about.title: Monrovia Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Monrovia's traffic moves fast where the 210 Freeway meets local streets like Huntington and Foothill, and that mix produces real consequences — 193 injury collisions and 263 people hurt in the most recent year on record, with Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. seeing the heaviest crash activity. If you were injured in one of these collisions, what happens in the days right after matters. Los Angeles County insurers often move quickly to get injured drivers on record before they've seen a doctor or talked to anyone else. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney in the network who can look at your situation, explain your options under California law, and help you avoid mistakes that could affect a future claim. There's no obligation to move forward, and no fee owed unless your attorney recovers something for you.

items.title: California's Clock Doesn't Pause
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city vehicle or a defect in a public road — is involved. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Bar You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly responsible for the crash — your share of fault simply reduces the amount. Insurers sometimes use this rule to talk injured drivers into lowball settlements, so it helps to have someone reviewing the numbers on your behalf.

items.title: No Cap Means Your Story Matters
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, so the full impact of your injury can be part of the conversation. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out what your claim may be worth.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's generally best not to give a recorded statement to the other side's insurer before speaking with an attorney. These calls are often used to lock in details that can later be used to reduce or deny your claim. An independent attorney can advise you on what to say, if anything, before you respond.

items.question: What if my accident happened on I-210 near Monrovia and I'm not sure who's at fault?
items.answer: Fault on a freeway corridor like I-210 can involve multiple factors — following distance, lane changes, or road conditions near the Huntington and Foothill interchanges. California's comparative fault rule means you can still pursue a claim even if fault is shared. An attorney can help gather evidence, such as traffic camera footage or witness statements, to sort out what happened.

items.question: How much does it cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects injured people with independent attorneys in California, including Monrovia. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if they recover money for you.
